title: U.S. House · Missouri's 8th District
area: Southeast Missouri, the Bootheel and the Ozarks, including Cape Girardeau, Poplar Bluff and West Plains.

context.text: Incumbent Jason Smith won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary over Gordon Heslop. Christopher Reichard won the Democratic primary over Frank Barnitz. Rebecca Sharpe Lombard advanced unopposed in the Libertarian primary.

candidates.name: Jason Smith
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2013); Chairman, House Committee on Ways and Means

summary.text: Jason Smith is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Missouri's 8th District and chairs the House Committee on Ways and Means. He was an attorney, real estate agent and small-business owner and served in the Missouri House from 2005 to 2013 before winning a 2013 special election to Congress. His congressional website describes him as a seventh-generation Missourian who is a fourth-generation owner of his family's farm.

background.text: Born in St. Louis in 1980 and raised in Salem, Missouri; attended Salem High School, where according to his congressional website he was active in FFA.
Earned degrees in Agricultural Economics and Business Administration from the University of Missouri-Columbia, according to his website, then a J.D. from Oklahoma City University (2004).
Worked as an attorney, real estate agent and small-business owner before holding public office; his website also describes him as a fourth-generation owner of his family's farm.
Served in the Missouri House of Representatives (District 120) from 2005 to 2013, rising to Speaker Pro Tem according to his website.
Was chosen by the Missouri Republican Party as its nominee in the 2013 special election to replace Jo Ann Emerson and won the June 4, 2013 general election with 67.1% of the vote.

In Congress, sat on the Judiciary and Natural Resources committees in 2013-2014 and on Ways and Means from 2015; was Conference Secretary of the House Republican leadership during President Trump's first term, and became the top Republican on the House Budget Committee in 2021, according to his website.

Became chairman of the Ways and Means Committee in January 2023; according to his website, he was the youngest chair in modern times at age 42. In 2025-2026 he also chairs the Joint Committee on Taxation.
According to his website, led the committee's work on the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, signed July 4, 2025.
Won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary with 86.0% of the vote over Gordon Heslop.
According to his congressional website, he attends Grace Community Church in Salem.

priorities.text: Official House issues page organizes his stated priorities around veterans ("American Heroes"), healthcare freedom, agriculture ("Focused on Farms"), deregulation ("Keeping Washington Out of Missouri"), and lower taxes ("Your Money Belongs in Your Pocket").

positions.summary: Says healthcare decisions are personal and that "the government should not be sitting in the exam room with you and your doctor," favoring healthcare freedom and choice over government involvement.
Says people should be able to keep the money they earn rather than having it directed by "some bureaucrat in Washington," and says he works to roll back federal regulations.

record.text: Chairs the House Committee on Ways and Means and the Joint Committee on Taxation in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Served in the Missouri House of Representatives representing District 120 from 2005 to 2013.

candidates.name: Christopher Reichard

summary.text: Christopher (Chris) Reichard is the Democratic nominee for Missouri's 8th District. An Army veteran who served three tours in Iraq, he became a union electrician with IBEW Local 1 after working in non-union telecommunications construction. He is campaigning on strengthening organized labor and restoring cut federal programs.

background.text: Born in Tennessee and raised in the greater St. Louis region; joined the workforce at 16 and graduated from Northwest High School, according to his Ballotpedia survey and profile.
Enlisted in the U.S. Army at 18 and served from 2004 to 2012, including three tours in Iraq.
After the Army, worked in non-union telecommunications construction in Houston, Texas, before returning home and joining IBEW Local 1 as a union electrician.
Ballotpedia lists his profession as communications specialist.
Won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary with 54.1% of the vote over Frank Barnitz; this is his first run for office listed by Ballotpedia.

priorities.text: Labor: says his primary goal is strengthening the working class by removing restrictions on unions that he says have held them back since 1947 (a reference to the Taft-Hartley Act).
Says he wants to restore federal departments and programs he says were cut, including re-establishing what he calls healthy trade policies.
Says he aims to protect and defend the Constitution and reinforce checks and balances among the branches of government.

candidates.researchNotes: No prior elected office; positions drawn from his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. A stated position on the minimum wage was removed because his survey response addresses union strength generally, not minimum-wage policy specifically.

candidates.name: Rebecca Sharpe Lombard
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Libertarian primary

summary.text: Rebecca Sharpe Lombard is the Libertarian Party nominee for Missouri's 8th District. She describes herself as a Tower Grove South resident who works in IT, with degrees in math and public policy. She ran for the Missouri House in 2022.

background.text: Describes herself as having grown up in rural Missouri and lived in the Tower Grove South neighborhood of St. Louis for about 20 years.
Describes having degrees in math and public policy, working in IT, and experience in teaching, finance and contracts.
Was the Libertarian candidate for Missouri House District 80 in 2022, receiving 3.1% (329 votes) in a race won by incumbent Peter Merideth.
Advanced from the August 4, 2026 Libertarian primary unopposed.
